threshold_source: Schröder et al. 2013: 0-4 subclinical, 5-9 mild, 10-14 moderate, 15-19 severe, 20-24 extreme. >=10 is also the Youden-optimal cut-off against functional impairment (WSAS >=9) in Möllmann et al. 2023 (10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1112472): AUC 0.86, sensitivity 0.89, specificity 0.67
notes: Naylor et al. 2021 call >=5 'clinically significant' (49.1%); by our rule that is L1. Any threshold below 5 (e.g., 'score 1-24 = misophonia') is L0. Completed by an interviewer, the scale keeps these levels (rule G7)

full_name: Misophonia Questionnaire (Symptom Scale, Emotions and Behaviors Scale, Misophonia Severity Scale)
score_range: MSS 1-15 (0 = no sound sensitivity); total of the Symptom and Emotions-and-Behaviors scales 0-68
L1_rule: MSS >=4 (mild or more); Symptom Scale >=14 (mean item >=2)
L2_rule: MSS >=7 (recommended); total >=30; Emotions-and-Behaviors scale >=19; MSS >=7 and Emotions-and-Behaviors mean >=2
threshold_source: MSS bands minimal 1-3, mild 4-6, moderate 7-9, severe 10-12, very severe 13-15 (Wu et al. 2014, quoted by Rosenthal et al. 2021, 10.3389/fpsyg.2021.709928). Möllmann et al. 2023 (10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1112472), Youden-optimal against functional impairment: MSS >=7 (sensitivity 0.78, specificity 0.77), total >=30 or >=31, Emotions-and-Behaviors >=19, >=20 or >=21 (equal Youden index). MSS >=7 plus Emotions-and-Behaviors mean >=2: conservative clinical criterion of Rosenthal et al. 2021
verified_2026_10_09: yes (Wu 2014 by secondary quotation, primary paper closed); Rosenthal 2021 and Möllmann 2023 full texts read 2026-10-15
notes: Symptom Scale >=14 has no clinical anchoring; Jakubovski et al. 2022 use it as a screen for people 'sometimes' sensitive -> L1. Thresholds above an L2 cut-off (e.g., total >=34, MSS >=11) are L2 (rule G2)

threshold_source: Siepsiak, Sobczak et al. 2020 (10.3390/ijerph17155464), anchored on face-to-face interview
notes: Subsets of MisoQuest items with a study-defined threshold: rule G3 (L1). Top 20% of a sample or other percentiles: E3 (rule G5)

threshold_source: Vitoratou et al. 2023 (10.1371/journal.pone.0282777), ROC against semi-structured interview
notes: In Vitoratou et al. 2023 the cut-off was derived in the same sample (ROC against the interview subsample): estimate kept at L2 and flagged (rule G8)

threshold_source: Simner et al. 2024, ROC: self-declared misophonics vs general population
notes: Also reported as 'SMS'. In Simner et al. 2024 the cut-off was derived in the same sample (general-population positive rate = 1 - specificity): kept at L2 and flagged (rule G8)

threshold_source: Rinaldi et al. 2022: 90th percentile of their sample, close to adult 50.5
notes: in Rinaldi et al. 2022 itself the estimate is percentile-defined -> E3, not pooled; this applies to the same Multisense sample in any other report (rule G5); in other samples L2, excluded in sensitivity analysis 2

L1_rule: subclinical or clinical (symptom criteria met, with or without the impairment criterion)
L2_rule: clinical: meets all symptom criteria + impairment criterion (algorithm)
notes: approximates the 2022 consensus definition except duration

score_range: Symptom Severity composite: 23 items 0-4 (total 0-92, or mean item score); Impairment scale total 0-48
L2_rule: Symptom Severity mean >=1.8 or total >=41.4 (recommended); Impairment total >=14 (moderate or more); Impairment total >=39 (severe to very severe)
threshold_source: Rosenthal et al. 2021, Results: Youden-optimal cut point of 1.8 (total 41.4) separating clinical from subclinical misophonia, criterion MQ MSS >=7 and Emotions-and-Behaviors mean >=2; AUC 0.97, sensitivity 1.00, specificity 0.91. Impairment ranges 0-13 minimal-mild, 14-38 moderate, 39-48 severe to very severe, set on percentiles of the development sample matched to MQ MSS ranges
notes: Corrects the entry of 2026-10-09, which said Rosenthal et al. 2021 give no DMQ cut-off; the cut-offs are in their Results. In the development sample (Rosenthal et al. 2021) estimates on the percentile-based Impairment ranges are E3 (rule G5)

L2_rule: none (no clinical cut-off published by developers)
threshold_source: Remmert et al. 2022: 'A clinical cutoff must be determined'
notes: L1 only unless a later validation gives an interview-anchored cut-off. Not used by any included study (checked 2026-10-15)

L2_rule: >=24 (Youden-optimal; recommended; equals '>23' of Jakubovski et al. 2022); >=21 (moderate to severe or more)
threshold_source: Severity key 0-10 normal/subclinical, 11-20 mild, 21-30 moderate to severe, 31-40 severe to extreme: tabulated as the existing categorization in Möllmann et al. 2023 (10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1112472), Table 1, and used with the Turkish validation (Cakiroglu et al. 2022, 10.1521/bumc.2022.86.2.159; abstract read, full text closed). Not printed on the AMISOS-R form (Jager et al. 2020, S3 Appendix). Möllmann et al. 2023: >=23 or >=24 against functional impairment (AUC 0.84; equal Youden index)
verified_2026_10_09: yes (2026-10-15: AMISOS-R form, Jager 2020 and Möllmann 2023 full texts; Cakiroglu 2022 abstract)
notes: No interview-anchored cut-off. Jakubovski et al. 2022 derived '>23' from the mean minus 1 SD of Jager et al.'s patients; an external sample, so not E3

L1_rule: >=12 (mild or more, band version A); >=11 (mild or more, band version B with a subclinical band)
L2_rule: >=25 (moderate or more, version A); >=22 (moderate or more, version B); >=24 (Youden-optimal, Möllmann et al. 2023)
threshold_source: Version A, as reported by Aryal & Prabhu 2022 (10.31117/neuroscirn.v5i4.161): 0-11 subclinical, 12-24 mild, 25-37 moderate, 38-50 severe, 51-63 extreme. Version B, the existing categorization in Möllmann et al. 2023 (10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1112472): mild 0-21, moderate 22-42, severe 43-63 (some studies split off a subclinical band below 10 or 11). Möllmann et al. 2023: >=24 against functional impairment (AUC 0.87, sensitivity 0.81, specificity 0.77)
verified_2026_10_09: yes (secondary sources; Möllmann 2023 full text read 2026-10-15)
notes: Band thresholds (>=22, >=25) are not anchored to an interview or ROC: JBI 6 = no, so L2 estimates on MAQ bands are excluded in sensitivity analysis 2; >=24 is ROC-anchored. Sums inside the subclinical band (e.g., MpAQ >=2) are L0
Not used by any included study (checked 2026-10-15)

full_name: Clinical or (semi-)structured interview with explicit criteria (Schröder 2013, Jager 2020, Swedo 2022 consensus, Duke Misophonia Interview, Misophonia Interview Schedule (Kılıç et al. 2021), Misophonia Interview Scale with Öz criteria, Pre-OK-SCIM (Vitoratou et al. 2023), study-specific stated criteria)
notes: L3 needs criteria stated in the report or in a cited source, applied by a clinician or trained interviewer; study-specific criteria must be stated in full, otherwise L1 (e.g., clinician judgement with unstated 'clinical questions'). A category that merges misophonia with phonophobia or another sound intolerance (Structured Tinnitus Interview 'phonophobia/misophonia') is not misophonia-specific: E2 at the estimate level, listed, not pooled (rule G9). Interview items that only record a trigger (e.g., 'at least one sound rated moderate') are L0

full_name: Single or ad hoc items written for the study, or unvalidated short screeners
L1_rule: self-identified misophonia (with or without a definition shown); self-reported earlier professional diagnosis; frequency items at 'often' or 'more than half of the days' or above; intensity items (e.g., 'does the sound of chewing fill you with rage?'); symptom counts on ad hoc item sets
L2_rule: only if the item set requires both the misophonic reaction and distress or impairment (e.g., Kurztest Misophonie with impairment >=3/10)
notes: L0 (described, not pooled): items asking only about any bothersome, disturbing or 'sensitive to' sound, or any trigger. Within L1, self-identification, self-reported diagnosis and single items are used only when the sample has no scale-based L1 estimate. JBI 6 = no for every ad hoc definition

full_name: Decreased Sound Tolerance Scale - Screening, misophonia section (MTS)
threshold_source: Alluşoğlu & Aksoy 2022: ROC against participants' self-assignment to sound-intolerance types; cut-off chosen for about 85% sensitivity: sensitivity 0.861, specificity 0.623
notes: A screening cut-off, not a clinical-significance cut-off -> L1. Factor subscale thresholds have no published basis (rule G3)

full_name: Misophonia Screening List - Child and Youth (child and parent report)
threshold_source: Rappoldt et al. 2024: ROC, 94 youth with misophonia from the Amsterdam UMC clinical sample (trial NL-OMON20775) vs school controls; child report AUC 0.958, sensitivity 0.968, specificity 0.770; parent report AUC 0.990, sensitivity 0.968, specificity 0.949
notes: In Rappoldt et al. 2024 the positive rate in the initial control group equals 1 - specificity: kept at L2 and flagged (rule G8)

full_name: Sound Sensitivity Symptoms Questionnaire, item 4 (anger or anxiety at eating, breathing and similar sounds)
threshold_source: Aazh et al. 2022 (instrument). No misophonia cut-off published; level by the frequency rule of the adhoc row

score_range: agrees or disagrees with a characterization of misophonia; disruption of daily life: not at all / very mildly / moderately / severely / very severely
L2_rule: agrees and rates disruption of daily life at least 'very mildly' (developers' definition)
threshold_source: Rinaldi & Simner 2023: convergent and divergent validity; no interview or ROC anchoring
notes: L2 by the adhoc rule (reaction plus impairment); JBI 6 = no; excluded in sensitivity analysis 2
